panel.introduction: At the center of our solar system, the Sun is a 4.5-billion-year-old yellow dwarf star. Its light and heat make life on Earth possible.

controls.label: Photosphere
controls.description: Colorized HMI continuum mosaic for Carrington Rotation 2311, 12 May–9 June 2026. It combines different observation dates; limb normalization and polar continuation are prepared display adjustments.
controls.title: HMI continuum mosaic CR2311
controls.summary: Visible-light observations span May–June 2026. Color and brightness are adjusted; missing polar coverage is filled.

controls.label: Magnetic field
controls.description: False-color HMI radial magnetic field for Carrington Rotation 2311, 12 May–9 June 2026. A synoptic mosaic, not a simultaneous photograph; weak and strong fields use a nonlinear color scale.
controls.title: HMI radial magnetic field CR2311
controls.summary: Colors show the radial field on a nonlinear scale. Measurements span May–June 2026 rather than a single instant.

controls.label: Chromosphere
controls.description: False-color AIA 304 Å synoptic mosaic, 12 May–9 June 2026. Missing samples use latitude continuation. The stationary off-limb image is a separate observation from 27 May 2026.
controls.title: AIA 304 Å synoptic map CR2311
controls.summary: The 304 Å measurements span May–June 2026. Gaps use nearby latitudes; the separate outer image is from 27 May.

controls.label: Corona
controls.description: False-color AIA 171 Å synoptic mosaic, 12 May–9 June 2026. Missing samples use latitude continuation. The stationary off-limb image is a separate observation from 27 May 2026.
controls.title: AIA 171 Å synoptic map CR2311
controls.summary: The 171 Å measurements span May–June 2026. Gaps use nearby latitudes; the separate outer image is from 27 May.
